content.summary: The literal extremal statement, empty-core convention, attribution of the principal imports, and ordinary-versus-formal assurance framing are clear. Round 1 copy review requires two concrete repairs: restore missing prose spacing throughout, and replace or define the undeclared scalar neighbourhood notation N. A bounded comparison with the pinned prior manuscript found attributed shared theorem language and bibliography, without a specific uncredited prose passage; this is not a comprehensive text-reuse clearance or mathematical acceptance.
required_revisions: Restore ordinary word/number, label/number, date, and bibliographic spacing throughout the manuscript, including 'at most67', 'our24October2026', 'Theorem1', 'Proposition6.7', 'commit90c03...', and 'Computing2(4),479–490,1993'. Preserve all numerical values and mathematical signs during this editorial pass.

Define the scalar neighbourhood shorthand used in Sections 5.1 and 6, or replace N≤46, N≤45, N≤44, and N≤43 by explicit universally quantified bounds on |N[R]|. Define an 'N43 anchor' as an actual member R with |N[R]|=43. Keep N[R] as the set already defined in Section 3, so the minimum-degree deduction cannot be read as following merely from a bound on the minimum neighbourhood.

findings.statement: Missing spaces are pervasive in prose, theorem labels, dates, and references; examples occur at manuscript lines 5, 13, 23, 25, 27, 31 and throughout the references. These are editorial defects rather than evidence of a changed numerical theorem.
findings.disposition: Complete a global spacing pass and verify that every formula and numerical constant remains unchanged.

findings.statement: Section 3 defines the set N[R] and its minimum size μ, but Sections 5.1 and 6 use an undeclared scalar N and the phrase 'N43 anchor'. The deduction of graph minimum degree 25 in Section 6 requires |N[R]|≤43 for every actual R.
findings.disposition: Make the universal quantifier and scalar cardinality explicit. The cap15 companion supplies the intended universal meaning, so this is a repairable exposition defect, not a demonstrated false deduction.

findings.statement: The manuscript correctly bounds its novelty statement by the located-source search and distinguishes imported H27/Jin and shared-builder exact checks from end-to-end Lean assurance.
findings.disposition: Retain these qualifications in all later abstracts, summaries, and publication metadata.

findings.statement: The accessible pinned October 9 source and current manuscript share standard definition/theorem language and bibliographic strings. The source is expressly credited in Section 2; the bounded comparison did not identify a specific unattributed distinctive prose passage.
findings.disposition: This finding covers the inspected pinned main.tex only. Do not describe it as plagiarism-free certification, exhaustive originality verification, or comparison with inaccessible source text.

checks.method: Computed SHA-256 of manuscript.md and of snapshot.json serialized as sorted compact UTF-8 JSON with ensure_ascii=False; inspected the roster entry.
checks.observation: The manuscript hash is 2c200bf5dff9e665e7dab3ba3f5a1ef019251d341a1913d1f5bd2fc3c086f937 and the canonical snapshot hash is 7912a1f1de1f27d72b2a2e660626f338303bf8cf71085720b4c1e304e670b5ba, matching the assignment. The roster role is copyeditor for /root/r67_copy.

checks.scope: Literal statement and convention in Abstract and Sections 1–3
checks.method: Read the complete frozen manuscript and compared its definitions and threshold convention with the pinned prior paper, paper/main.tex, introduction and notation sections.
checks.observation: The present manuscript explicitly uses maximum sunflower-free size M(4,3), exact uniformity four, distinct members, arbitrary used support, and forbidden empty cores. Its forcing cardinality 68 consistently corresponds to upper bound 67; the prior paper's forcing cardinality 69 corresponds to upper bound 68.

checks.scope: Neighbourhood notation in manuscript lines 35, 113, 147 and 165
checks.method: Compared every manuscript occurrence of scalar N with D16-complete-argument.md and LOW15-complete-argument.md, especially the latter's upstream route item 5.
checks.observation: Only N[R] as a set and μ as its minimum cardinality are defined in the manuscript. LOW15-complete-argument.md explicitly says every actual neighbourhood has size at most 43, confirming the intended universal bound needed for graph minimum degree 25. The manuscript shorthand omits this definition.

checks.method: Read the pinned prior paper's abstract, introduction and notation sections, then ran a cheap whole-file normalized token SequenceMatcher comparison between its paper/main.tex and the frozen manuscript, stripping TeX command names and normalizing letter/number boundaries.
checks.observation: The longest returned matching block was a 20-token bibliographic title/author string; the next was a 16-token fragment of the attributed Jin theorem. Another 11-token overlap states the attributed intersecting upper bound 27. This bounded method found no concrete uncredited distinctive prose passage, but token normalization and one-source coverage do not establish absence of all reuse.

checks.scope: Novelty and imported-source language in Sections 1–2, 5.2 and 7–8
checks.method: Compared the manuscript's descriptions with EXTERNAL-H27-JIN-SCOPE.md, FOUNDATION_LEDGER.md, FRONTIER_REFRESH.md and R15ScalarClosure-status.md.
checks.observation: The text preserves H27's unreplayed external ledger boundary, selected six-of-42 prior-suite scope, Jin access through Nikiforov, the bounded negative literature observation, and the five arithmetic roots' restricted formal scope. The fifteen-triple lemma's separate global novelty is expressly disclaimed in Section 5.2.
